producer_report.summary: I added a model-free design-surface inventory and diff to athena-core, plus a new `athena.design-surface/1` record, with tests. `inventory_at(git, commit)` reads five sources from the commit's tree, not the working tree. These are the clap definitions in main.rs, the config structs in config.rs, the `AnyRecord` serde renames, the `RoleDefinition` literals in roles.rs, and the workspace members. It returns sorted maps for commands, flags, config keys, record schemas, roles and crates, so the same commit gives the same bytes. `diff(old, new)` returns added, removed and changed lists per kind, and `totals()` sums them. A section added or removed counts as one item, with its key count in the detail (for example `section (2 keys)`). Without that, one removed section would have counted once per key and could not match the brief's "one removed config section". `Athena::record_design_surface(commit, now)` commits the record at `records/design-surface/<month>/<id>.json`. No CLI command was added. The new `AnyRecord` variant is wired into `parse`, `canonical_path` and `schema`, and into the store's `Records` loader. Tests in athena-core, athena-data and athena-cli cover the two-commit diff, determinism, the HEAD agreement checks and the record round trip. The docs section and the CHANGELOG entry are written.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test builds a temporary git repository with two commits (a CLI command added, an athena.toml section removed, a record schema moving to version 2) and asserts the diff reports exactly those three changes (one added command, one removed config section, one changed record schema) and nothing else, with totals of 3.
criteria_check.evidence: design_surface::tests::a_command_added_a_section_removed_and_a_schema_moved_are_exactly_three_changes passed. It builds two commits in a temp repo and asserts the whole SurfaceDiff equals one added command, one removed config section and one changed record schema. It also asserts totals 1/1/1/3. The full `cargo test -p athena-core` run passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test computes the inventory at this repository's HEAD and asserts it contains every top-level subcommand of the clap Command that `athena --help` prints and every [section] header that the repository's athena.toml uses.
criteria_check.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/design_surface.rs::the_inventory_at_head_lists_every_command_in_help_and_every_section_athena_toml_uses passed. It runs the built binary with --help and parses the Commands list. It parses HEAD's athena.toml for every table path and checks each against the inventory.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test computes the inventory twice at the same commit and asserts the two results are equal and serialize to identical bytes.
criteria_check.evidence: Two tests passed: design_surface::tests::the_inventory_is_identical_when_computed_twice_at_one_commit in athena-core, and crates/athena-cli/tests/design_surface.rs::the_inventory_at_head_is_identical_when_computed_twice at this repo's HEAD. Both assert equality and identical serde_json bytes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean; `cargo test` passes as a whole including the records round-trip test that covers the new design-surface AnyRecord variant and check_record_file accepting it.

criteria_check.evidence: I did not edit config.rs or athena.toml. The athena-data repo_config tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the design-surface inventory and diff, and docs/records.md has a section describing the design-surface record: its schema string, fields, and how it is compared across commits.

The section gives the schema string `athena.design-surface/1`, the fields id/at/commit/inventory, the six kinds, and how `diff` compares across commits.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff has added, removed and changed lists per kind (commands, flags, config keys, record schemas, roles, crates) plus totals; Grep of the change shows no model/agent call in the inventory or diff code.
criteria_check.evidence: SurfaceDiff holds a KindDiff {added, removed, changed} for each of the six kinds, and `totals()` gives added/removed/changed/total. Grep of design_surface.rs for AgentDriver, `driver.` and model calls found 0 matches. The code only reads git blobs and parses them with syn and toml_edit.

open_issues: There is no command or hook that calls `record_design_surface`. The brief said to record via a function and add no subcommand, so a later job must decide when to call it.

Positional arguments are listed under `flags` with a `<name>` key, and their detail is the field's Rust type. A flag's long name comes from the field name or `long = ".."`. A clap `alias` or `rename_all` on an enum is not followed.
Config capability ids such as `[capabilities.change]` are map keys, so the inventory holds only `capabilities` and its fixed sub-keys. The HEAD test checks only the top-level section for those paths.
mistakes: My first test used `[surface.clone()]` for a slice comparison, which tripped the clippy lint cloned_ref_to_slice_refs. I fixed it.
I ran the full athena-core suite twice (about 5 minutes each) because the first run's output was truncated and I could not read the saved file.
learnings: The brief names `athena --help` as the source of the command list, but athena-core cannot reach the clap Command because athena-cli depends on core. The HEAD tests therefore live in crates/athena-cli/tests/design_surface.rs and run the built binary.
A new test file under crates/athena-cli/tests needs a line in xtask/shard-timings.txt.
code_health::tests::set_up and Git::isolated are reusable test scaffolds for athena-core; the athena-git testutil module is crate-private.
The producer shell allows no pipes, tail or cat, so test logs are read with --quiet or through the Read tool.
Adding an AnyRecord variant requires an arm in store.rs, or Records::load panics on job_of for the unmatched record.
desires: A way to read persisted tool output files so a large test log can be searched for failures; I reran with --quiet instead.
